context:
Evaluating a Coralogix support response for this user question:

Our APM dashboards stop loading beyond a few days. The worst offender is `duration_ms_bucket`, and the spanmetrics connector has these dimensions: `http.method`, `cgx.transaction`, `cgx.transaction.root`, `status_code`, `url.full`, `http.response.status_code`, plus Kubernetes pod labels. `url.full` alone has hundreds of thousands of values because it includes IDs and query strings. Should we just raise the cardinality limit, or is there a better fix?

checklist.name: mentions-cardinality-limit
checklist.description: The response matches the pattern: (?i)(aggregation_cardinality_limit|aggregationCardinalityLimit|cardinality limit|overflow)

checklist.name: root-cause-high-cardinality-dimensions
checklist.description: Identifies the root cause as high-cardinality Span Metrics dimensions, especially raw `url.full` and broad pod labels, and recommends removing or replacing them with bounded labels such as templated `http.route` before raising backend or collector limits.

checklist.name: guardrail-not-primary-fix
checklist.description: Explains that raising `aggregation_cardinality_limit` is only a guardrail or temporary mitigation; the durable fix is to normalize/sanitize dynamic IDs before `spanmetrics` and trim dimensions. A response that only recommends raising the limit is a FAIL.
